<a id="materialnamepattern"></a>

## `MaterialNamePattern`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.MaterialNamePattern` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Material names with wildcards: `*` matches any run of characters (including none), `?` exactly one. Case-insensitive, like every other material-name match in the framework. `mt_env_*` is every window-view scenery material; `mt_desk*` is the desk family (which also matches `mt_desktop` and `mt_desk_lamp` - name them exactly when that matters).

<a id="materialnamepattern--ispattern"></a>

### `static bool IsPattern(string pattern)`

True when `pattern` contains a wildcard.

**Parameters**

- `pattern`: A material name or pattern.

<a id="materialnamepattern--matches"></a>

### `static bool Matches(string pattern, string name)`

True when `name` matches `pattern`.

**Parameters**

- `pattern`: A name or a wildcard pattern; null or blank matches nothing.
- `name`: A material's base name (no `" (Instance)"` suffix); null matches nothing.

## `MaterialPropertyRule`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.MaterialPropertyRule` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One material property change from `textures/_rules.json`: "set `_Color` on every loaded material named `mt_desk_1` to this colour". The scenery and desk counterpart of a [`TextureRule`](#texturerule): written on the shared material asset in memory, backed up first, put back by `TextureFeature.RestoreAll`. No game file is ever written.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser"></a>

## `MaterialPropertyRuleParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.MaterialPropertyRuleParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Reads the material *property* entries of `textures/_rules.json` - the entries that carry a value instead of a `file`:

```csharp
{ "material": "mt_desk_1", "property": "_Color", "tint": "#E8C9A8" }
{ "material": "mt_env_*", "property": "_Color", "color": [0.9, 0.95, 1.0] }
{ "material": "mt_env_buil", "property": "_EmissionColor", "color": "#FFD9A0", "intensity": 2.5 }
{ "material": "mt_desk_1", "property": "_MainTexHSVG", "vector": [0.05, 1.1, 1, 1] }
{ "material": "mt_env_aurora", "property": "_Contrast", "float": 0.8 }
```

Texture entries in the same file are [`TextureRuleParser`](#textureruleparser)'s; each parser skips the other's entries in silence. A bad entry costs only that entry.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--keycolor"></a>

### `const string KeyColor = "color"`

An absolute colour.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--keyfloat"></a>

### `const string KeyFloat = "float"`

A float.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--keyintensity"></a>

### `const string KeyIntensity = "intensity"`

HDR multiplier for `color`/`tint` (rgb only).

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--keytint"></a>

### `const string KeyTint = "tint"`

A colour multiplied onto the original.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--keyvector"></a>

### `const string KeyVector = "vector"`

A vector.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--fromrulesjson"></a>

### `static MaterialPropertyRuleSet FromRulesJson(string packId, string json)`

Reads every property entry of a `_rules.json`.

**Parameters**

- `packId`: The pack's id.
- `json`: The file's text; null or blank is an empty set.

**Returns:** The rules and a problem per rejected entry. Malformed JSON is reported by [`TextureRuleParser`](#textureruleparser), not twice.

**Exceptions**

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--ispropertyentry"></a>

- `entry`: One entry.

The other properties that hold the same colour, written too where the material declares them: lilToon and URP materials mirror `_Color` into `_BaseColor` (every scenery and desk material in game 1.17.3 carries both with the same value).

**Parameters**

- `property`: A resolved property.

<a id="materialpropertyruleparser--trycolor"></a>

### `static bool TryColor(object raw, out Float4 color, out string problem)`

Reads a colour: `"#RGB"`, `"#RRGGBB"`, `"#RRGGBBAA"`, or an array of three or four numbers (0 or more; above 1 is HDR). Alpha defaults to 1.

**Parameters**

- `raw`: The JSON value.

- `problem`: Why it is not a colour, or null.

**Returns:** True when read.

<a id="paidcontentguard"></a>

## `PaidContentGuard`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.PaidContentGuard` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Project rule: paid content is never modified, replaced, re-skinned or unlocked. This is the check every texture and material-property rule passes before it touches a material.

What the game marks as paid, as observed in game 1.17.3:

- Steam DLC: `NestopiSystem.Steam.BulbulSteamDLC.DLC_1 = 3718890` - the original soundtrack, audio only; `NestopiSystem.Steam.SteamManager.IsInstalledDLC` has no caller.
- Decorations and environments unlock through `UnlockItemService.ConditionsType` `None`/`Scenario`/`PointPurchase`: in-game points, not money (collaborations and exclusives are treated as free).
- Mobile-only store items (`DecorationSkinListItemModelForMobile.IsPurchased`) have no PC materials.

So no material of the PC build is paid today. The guard is the defence for a later DLC: a material whose name carries a store marker is refused, with one warning naming the rule. No material in game 1.17.3 matches these patterns (all 235 materials checked).

<a id="paidcontentguard--deniedpatterns"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> DeniedPatterns { get; }`

Material/renderer name patterns treated as paid content.

<a id="paidcontentguard--isrefused"></a>

### `static bool IsRefused(string name, out string reason)`

True when the name looks like paid content and must not be touched.

**Parameters**

- `name`: A material or renderer name, or a rule's material pattern.
- `reason`: The sentence for the warning, or null.

## `TextureFileSnapshot`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.TextureFileSnapshot` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What the texture files of the installed packs looked like at one moment: a path and the file's last-write stamp, for every PNG and `_rules.json` a pack ships.

This is the pure half of the live-reload loop. The Unity side reads the disk and applies the result; deciding *what moved* - which files changed, appeared or were deleted - happens here, where it is unit-tested off-engine.

<a id="textureruleparser"></a>

## `TextureRuleParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.TextureRuleParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Turns a pack's texture files into [`TextureRule`](#texturerule)s. Two sources, in this order:

1. the folder convention `textures/<RendererName>/<slot>.png`, where `slot` is a shader property (`_MainTex`) or an alias ([`TextureSlotAliases`](#textureslotaliases));
2. the optional `textures/_rules.json`, for the cases the folder layout cannot say: a material index other than 0, or a file whose name is not the slot.

The rules file is merged *after* the convention, so an explicit entry wins over a file that happens to sit in the matching folder.

A PNG that is not at exactly `textures/<folder>/<file>.png`, any file that is not a PNG, and anything under a folder whose name starts with [`TextureRuleParser.PrivateFolderPrefix`](#textureruleparser--privatefolderprefix), are all passed over in silence: packs legitimately keep source art, notes and the rules file itself under `textures/`. Only a file that clearly *meant* to be a rule and failed - an unknown slot name - becomes a [`TextureRuleProblem`](#textureruleproblem). The count of files seen versus rules made is logged, so a silent miss is still visible.

<a id="textureruleparser--privatefolderprefix"></a>

### `const char PrivateFolderPrefix = '_'`

A folder directly under `textures/` whose name starts with this is the pack author's own - source art, work in progress - and is never read as a renderer name.

<a id="textureruleparser--rulespath"></a>

### `const string RulesPath = "textures/_rules.json"`

Path of the optional advanced-mapping file, relative to the pack root.

<a id="textureruleparser--textureextension"></a>

### `const string TextureExtension = ".png"`

Extension a texture file must have; it is the only format the loader decodes.

<a id="textureruleparser--texturesfolder"></a>

### `const string TexturesFolder = "textures/"`

Folder every texture rule path starts with, with its trailing slash.

<a id="textureruleparser--build"></a>

### `static TextureRuleSet Build(string packId, IEnumerable<PackFile> files, string rulesJson)`

The pack's complete rule set: the folder convention with `_rules.json` layered on top, so an explicit entry overrides a conventional file for the same target.

**Parameters**

- `packId`: The pack's id.
- `files`: The pack's files; see [`TextureRuleParser.FromIndex`](#textureruleparser--fromindex).
- `rulesJson`: Text of `textures/_rules.json`, or null when the pack has none. The caller reads the file - Core never touches a filesystem.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `packId` is blank.

<a id="textureruleparser--fromindex"></a>

### `static TextureRuleSet FromIndex(string packId, IEnumerable<PackFile> files)`

Reads the folder convention out of a pack's file listing.

**Parameters**

- `packId`: The pack's id; stamped on every rule.
- `files`: The pack's files - `LoadedPack.Index.Files`, or just its `Textures`. Entries outside `textures/` are skipped, so either works. Null yields [`TextureRuleSet.Empty`](#textureruleset--empty).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `packId` is blank.

<a id="textureruleparser--frompath"></a>

### `static TextureRule FromPath(string packId, string relativePath, out TextureRuleProblem problem)`

Reads one path as a folder-convention rule.

**Parameters**

- `packId`: The pack's id.
- `relativePath`: A pack-relative path, any separator style.
- `problem`: Why the path was rejected when it looked like a rule and was not one; null when the path simply is not a texture rule (not a PNG, wrong depth, outside `textures/`).

**Returns:** The rule, or null.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `packId` is blank.

<a id="textureruleparser--fromrulesjson"></a>

### `static TextureRuleSet FromRulesJson(string packId, string json)`

Reads the optional `textures/_rules.json`: an array of `{"renderer":"Body","materialIndex":0,"property":"_MainTex","file":"my.png"}`.

`file` is relative to the `textures/` folder, so `"my.png"` is `textures/my.png` and `"Body/alt.png"` is `textures/Body/alt.png`. `property` accepts an alias just as a file stem does. `materialIndex` is optional and defaults to 0. A member the framework does not know is an error unless it starts with `x-`, which is reserved for the pack author.

**Parameters**

- `packId`: The pack's id.
- `json`: The whole text of the file; null or blank yields [`TextureRuleSet.Empty`](#textureruleset--empty).

**Returns:** The rules, plus a problem per rejected entry. Malformed JSON is one problem and no rules; a bad entry costs only that entry.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `packId` is blank.

<a id="textureruleset"></a>

## `TextureRuleSet`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.TextureRuleSet` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

An ordered, conflict-free set of [`TextureRule`](#texturerule)s, plus the files that could not become one.

"Conflict-free" is the whole point: two packs may both ship `textures/Body/_MainTex.png`, and exactly one of them can win. [`TextureRuleSet.Merge`](#textureruleset--merge-ienumerable-textureruleset) settles that by load order - the later pack overrides - and the loser is still visible in [`TextureRuleSet.Overridden`](#textureruleset--overridden) so a log line can say which pack lost and to whom, instead of a modder wondering why their texture does nothing.

The winner keeps the loser's *position* rather than moving to the end, so adding a pack that overrides one texture does not reshuffle every `TEXTURE` line in the log.

<a id="textureruleset--ctor"></a>

### `TextureRuleSet(IReadOnlyList<TextureRule> rules, IReadOnlyList<TextureRuleProblem> problems = null, IReadOnlyList<TextureRule> overridden = null)`

Creates a set. The rules must already be conflict-free; use [`TextureRuleSet.Merge`](#textureruleset--merge-ienumerable-textureruleset) otherwise.

**Parameters**

- `rules`: The rules, in apply order. Null means none.
- `problems`: Files that were rejected. Null means none.
- `overridden`: Rules that lost to a later pack. Null means none.

<a id="textureruleset--count"></a>

### `int Count { get; }`

How many rules will be applied.

<a id="textureruleset--empty"></a>

### `static TextureRuleSet Empty { get; }`

A set with nothing in it.

<a id="textureruleset--isempty"></a>

### `bool IsEmpty { get; }`

True when there is nothing to apply and nothing to complain about.

The distinct material names the rules mention, in first-seen order. Never null.

<a id="textureruleset--overridden"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<TextureRule> Overridden { get; }`

Rules that were replaced by a later pack's rule for the same [`TextureRule.Key`](#texturerule--key). Never null; always empty for a set that came straight out of one pack.

<a id="textureruleset--problems"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<TextureRuleProblem> Problems { get; }`

Files that could not become a rule, in the order they were read. Never null.

<a id="textureruleset--renderernames"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> RendererNames { get; }`

The distinct renderer names the rules mention, in first-seen order. Never null.

<a id="textureruleset--rules"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<TextureRule> Rules { get; }`

The rules, in the order they should be applied. Never null.

<a id="textureruleset--forrenderer"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<TextureRule> ForRenderer(string rendererName)`

Every rule targeting one renderer, in apply order. Never null.

**Parameters**

- `rendererName`: A renderer GameObject name; matched case-insensitively.

<a id="textureruleset--merge-textureruleset"></a>

### `static TextureRuleSet Merge(params TextureRuleSet[] orderedPacks)`

Merges sets given as arguments; see [`TextureRuleSet.Merge`](#textureruleset--merge-ienumerable-textureruleset).

**Parameters**

- `orderedPacks`: One set per pack, in load order.

<a id="textureruleset--merge-ienumerable-textureruleset"></a>

### `static TextureRuleSet Merge(IEnumerable<TextureRuleSet> orderedPacks)`

Merges per-pack rule sets into one, in load order: for a repeated [`TextureRule.Key`](#texturerule--key) the *last* set wins and the earlier rule moves to [`TextureRuleSet.Overridden`](#textureruleset--overridden). Problems from every set are kept, in order.

**Parameters**

- `orderedPacks`: One set per pack, in dependency/load order - the order `PackManager.Loaded` gives. Null entries are skipped; null itself yields [`TextureRuleSet.Empty`](#textureruleset--empty).

One line for LogOutput.log, e.g. `7 rule(s) over 3 renderer(s); 1 overridden; 2 problem(s)`.

Invariant culture, so the string is the same on every machine and in every test.

<a id="textureruletarget"></a>

## `TextureRuleTarget`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.TextureRuleTarget` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What a [`TextureRule`](#texturerule) names.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="textureruletarget--renderer"></a>`Renderer` | 0 | A renderer's GameObject name, e.g. `Body`. Written on that renderer's material at [`TextureRule.MaterialIndex`](#texturerule--materialindex). |

<a id="textureslotaliases"></a>

## `TextureSlotAliases`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.TextureSlotAliases` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Translates the friendly *slot* name a pack author writes into the shader property a material is actually keyed by.

A slot that starts with `_` is taken to be a shader property already and is passed through verbatim (after a spelling check), so a pack can reach any property this or a future shader has without waiting for an alias. Everything else must be in the table below.

The table is built from the shader and materials this game actually ships (game 1.17.3), not from lilToon's documentation:

- **base, main**: `_MainTex` (32) - `mt_Body._MainTex` = `t_body_base.png`
- **basemap**: `_BaseMap` (500) - hidden SRP mirror of `_MainTex`
- **basecolor**: `_BaseColorMap` (501) - hidden SRP mirror of `_MainTex`
- **main2, main3**: `_Main2ndTex` (40), `_Main3rdTex` (68)
- **shadow**: `_ShadowColorTex` (148) - lilToon's shadow colour slot; **unused** by this game's materials
- **shadow2, shadow3**: `_Shadow2ndColorTex` (154), `_Shadow3rdColorTex` (160)
- **shadowborder**: `_ShadowBorderMask` (139) - where `mt_Face`/`mt_Hair` put `*_shadow.png`
- **shadowstrength, shadowblur**: `_ShadowStrengthMask` (137), `_ShadowBlurMask` (141)
- **rim**: `_RimColorTex` (244) - `mt_Body._RimColorTex` = `t_body_shadow.png`
- **rimshade**: `_RimShadeMask` (174) - `mt_Hair._RimShadeMask` = `Hair_reflect.png`
- **backlight**: `_BacklightColorTex` (126) - `mt_Body._BacklightColorTex` = `t_body_shadow.png`
- **reflect, reflection**: `_ReflectionColorTex` (195) - `mt_Hair._ReflectionColorTex` = `Hair_reflect.png`
- **emission, emission2**: `_EmissionMap` (285), `_Emission2ndMap` (319)
- **normal, bump**: `_BumpMap` (99)
- **matcap, matcap2**: `_MatCapTex` (204), `_MatCap2ndTex` (224) - `mt_Hairpin` uses the 2nd
- **matcapmask, matcap2mask**: `_MatCapBlendMask` (211), `_MatCap2ndBlendMask` (231)
- **smoothness**: `_SmoothnessTex` (181) - `mt_Hairpin._SmoothnessTex`
- **metallic**: `_MetallicGlossMap` (183)
- **alphamask**: `_AlphaMask` (95)
- **outline**: `_OutlineTex` (472)

Note the one that surprises people: this game never fills `_ShadowColorTex`. The PNGs it calls "shadow" (`t_body_shadow.png`, `Face_2_shadow.png`, `Hair_shadow.png`) are bound to `_BacklightColorTex`, `_RimColorTex` and - on the face and hair - `_ShadowBorderMask`. Use `shadowborder`/`rim`/`backlight` to replace what the game shipped; `shadow` writes into a slot that was previously empty.

<a id="textureslotaliases--propertyprefix"></a>

### `const char PropertyPrefix = '_'`

The character a shader property name must start with.

<a id="textureslotaliases--aliases"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> Aliases { get; }`

Every alias, ordinally sorted. For the log line that lists what a pack may use.

<a id="textureslotaliases--maintexmirrors"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> MainTexMirrors { get; }`

lilToon's hidden SRP mirrors of `_MainTex` (lilToon.shader lines 500-501).

This game runs URP (its graphics settings name a `UniversalRenderPipelineAsset`, and the Managed folder ships the URP runtime), and every `mt_*` material binds the same texture to all three of `_MainTex`, `_BaseMap` and `_BaseColorMap`. Which one the URP pass samples cannot be told from outside - the game ships its 104 shaders compiled only - so a texture written to `_MainTex` alone may be sampled from a mirror that still holds the game's own texture. Writing all three costs nothing and removes the question.

<a id="textureslotaliases--iswellformedproperty"></a>

### `static bool IsWellFormedProperty(string name)`

True when `name` spells a shader property: `_` then word characters.

**Parameters**

- `name`: A candidate property name.

<a id="textureslotaliases--mirrorsof"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> MirrorsOf(string property)`

The other properties that should carry the same texture as `property`, or an empty list when it has none.

**Parameters**

- `property`: A resolved shader property, e.g. `_MainTex`.

<a id="textureslotaliases--resolve"></a>

### `static string Resolve(string slot)`

The shader property for a slot, or null when the slot is not understood.

**Parameters**

- `slot`: A file stem such as `base` or `_MainTex`.

<a id="textureslotaliases--tryresolve"></a>

### `static bool TryResolve(string slot, out string property, out string reason)`

Resolves a slot to a shader property.

**Parameters**

- `slot`: A file stem such as `base` or `_MainTex`. Aliases are case-insensitive; an explicit property keeps the author's casing, because Unity's material property lookup is case-sensitive.
- `property`: The shader property, or null when the slot is not understood.
- `reason`: Why it was not understood, or null on success.

**Returns:** True when `slot` named a usable property.

<a id="texturewritemode"></a>

## `TextureWriteMode`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Textures.TextureWriteMode` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which material a rule writes.

This exists because of what the first in-game run of texture replacement found: writing the renderer's *instance* material is correct and provably applied, and still changes nothing on screen when the renderer we found is not the one being drawn. `Bulbul.CostumeChangeService` deactivates the five default costume objects (`Body`, `Bottom1`, `Paka1`, `Socks`, `Top1`) and instantiates a costume prefab whose renderers have different names (`Body1`, `Top3`, `Bottom2`) but share the same material assets - `Body1` uses `mt_Body`, the very material `Body` uses.

So the shared material is the thing both renderers actually have in common, and writing it reaches the costume the player is wearing. It is an in-memory write to a loaded asset: no game file is touched, and `TextureFeature.RestoreAll` undoes it like any other.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="texturewritemode--instance"></a>`Instance` | 0 | Write `renderer.materials[i]` only. Affects exactly this renderer, and nothing else that happens to use the same material - but misses a renderer we never found. |
| <a id="texturewritemode--shared"></a>`Shared` | 1 | Write `renderer.sharedMaterials[i]` only. Reaches every renderer using that material, including ones the name lookup cannot see, and survives a costume swap that re-assigns `sharedMaterial`. |
| <a id="texturewritemode--both"></a>`Both` | 2 | Write both. The default while the costume interaction is being characterised. |
